第 29 章 Focus on Growth to Improve Employee Engagement关注成长以提升员工敬业度

Amy Rich / 艾米·里奇

— 第 88 页 —

Managers often miss one of their employees' core intrinsic motivators: clearly identifying their growth paths. Taking time to set bidirectional expectations in a professional development plan shows that you, as their manager, are invested in their success, resulting in better engagement and performance, greater job satisfaction, and retention. Within 30 days of a new person joining my team, we take at least an hour to go through a document that contains the questions we look at here in a moment, helping me understand what makes them tick and setting expectations about their growth path over the next year.

经理们经常忽略员工的核心内在动力之一：明确识别他们的成长路径。花时间在职业发展计划中设定双向期望，表明你作为经理在投资他们的成功，从而带来更好的敬业度和绩效、更高的工作满意度和留任率。新人加入我的团队 30 天内，我们会花至少一个小时过一份文档，里面包含我们稍后要看的问题，帮我了解他们的动力所在，并设定下一年成长路径的期望。

What Is a Professional Development Plan?什么是职业发展计划？

A professional development plan is more than a random document of vague skills that an employee might aspire to learn.

职业发展计划不只是一份随便列着员工可能想学的模糊技能的文档。

  • It's a holistic plan that melds the desires and needs of both you and the company and increases your ability to perform in your current job and/or your potential to perform in future roles.它是一个整体计划，融合你和公司双方的愿望和需求，提升你在当前工作中的表现能力和/或未来角色中的表现潜力。
  • It's not focused solely on technical skills or just about conferences and training.它不只关注技术技能，也不只是关于会议和培训。
  • It's not just about promotions (not everyone wants to advance beyond their current level).它不只是关于晋升（不是每个人都想超越当前级别发展）。

The questions that follow are meant to help you discover where you want to go over the next year (or longer!). What do you like or hate doing? What are you good at? How do you measure up to your job level, and where could you improve to meet or exceed expectations? We'll create a concrete action plan to help get you there.

以下问题旨在帮你发现你明年（或更久）想去哪里。你喜欢或讨厌做什么？你擅长什么？你如何对照你的工作级别衡量自己？你可以在哪里改进以达到或超越期望？我们会创建一个具体的行动计划帮你到达那里。

— 第 89 页 —

What motivates you?/What are your values? This helps identify the kinds of things that you want to focus on because they're important to you. This includes intrinsic motivators as well as specific work activities.

什么激励你？/你的价值观是什么？这有助于识别你想专注的事情类型，因为它们对你重要。这包括内在动力以及具体的工作活动。

What demotivates you?/What don't you want to do? This helps identify the kinds of things that you don't want to spend much time doing, because they make you unhappy. Again, include intrinsic demotivators as well as specific types of work tasks.

什么让你失去动力？/你不想做什么？这有助于识别你不想花太多时间做的事情类型，因为它们让你不快乐。同样，包括内在的去动力因素以及具体的工作任务类型。

What are your strengths? Be generous with yourself; tell me all of the awesome qualities you bring to work. Start by thinking of the things that you like (from above) that you're good at. Read this article for ideas about "soft skills," and also include your technical and business skills.

你的优势是什么？对自己大方一点；告诉我你带给工作的所有了不起的品质。从想你喜欢（从上面）且擅长的事情开始。读这篇文章了解「软技能」的思路，也包括你的技术和业务技能。

What are your goals? What are the results you want to see by this time next year? Are there specific technical or business skills that you want to learn? Do you want to be promoted? What specific impact do you want to have on your team or the business?

你的目标是什么？明年这个时候你想看到什么结果？有什么想学的特定技术或业务技能吗？你想晋升吗？你想对团队或业务产生什么具体影响？

What's our concrete action plan for getting you there? These are concrete specifics of how to reach those goals. They can include education/training opportunities, projects you're interested in leading or working on, relationships you want to build, etc. We'll also specify how I can help you achieve those things and hold you accountable.

我们让你到达那里的具体行动计划是什么？这些是如何达成目标的具体细节。可以包括教育/培训机会、你感兴趣主导或参与的项目、你想建立的关系等。我们还会明确我怎么帮你实现这些以及如何让你负责。

We dig deep, using the Five Why's, to get a really clear picture of the person's motivators, demotivators, and goals. Knowing this information attunes me to the needs of each employee and allows me to be a better manager for them, specifically. When we talk about the strengths section, some people tend to focus on just one of technical, leadership, or business skills and need a push to think about how well rounded they are across multiple dimensions. Using all of this information and my knowledge about what the team needs to succeed over the next year, we build a concrete, living action plan with specific (often prioritized) tasks.

我们用五个为什么深入挖掘，得到一个人动力、去动力因素和目标的清晰图景。知道这些信息让我能调准每个员工的需求，让我能 specifically 做他们更好的经理。当我们谈优势部分时，有些人倾向于只关注技术、领导力或业务技能中的一个，需要推一把来思考他们在多个维度上的全面性。用所有这些信息和我对团队明年成功需要什么的了解，我们建立一个具体的、活的行动计划，带具体（通常排序的）任务。

— 第 90 页 —

We check back on their progress every month, and if there are performance problems, the skills required by the company shift, or they decide to focus on something different, we add/modify/delete items from the plan. We also use progress notes as one part of a continuous feedback loop and roll them up to the person's six-month reviews. This, along with regular discussions about competencies as measured by our job ladder, ensures that the employee always knows where they stand, where they're going, and what skills to focus on to get there.

我们每个月检查他们的进展，如果有绩效问题、公司需要的技能转变、或者他们决定专注于不同的事情，我们就添加/修改/删除计划中的项目。我们还把进展记录作为持续反馈循环的一部分，汇总到这个人的六个月评估中。这加上关于职业阶梯衡量的能力的定期讨论，确保员工始终知道自己处于什么位置、要去哪里、以及需要专注什么技能才能到达那里。

If you aren't already creating professional development plans with your employees, try starting here, and see whether their engagement improves.

如果你还没有和员工一起创建职业发展计划，试试从这里开始，看看他们的敬业度是否改善。
